title: What Is a UPI ID? Meaning, How to Create, Find, and Change It
summary: Everything you need to know about UPI IDs - from creating and managing a UPI ID to accepting payments securely as an individual or business.

Table of Contents


Toggle


### Key Takeaways


- A UPI ID, also called a Virtual Payment Address or VPA, is a unique payment address linked to a bank account.
- A UPI ID usually contains a name or number followed by a payment handle, such as **yourname@oksbi** . It is different from a UPI Number, which is an 8 to 10-digit payment alias.
- You can share your UPI ID to receive money, but you must never share your UPI PIN or enter it to receive a payment.
- Google Pay does not directly edit an existing UPI ID. You can add an available ID for the linked bank account and remove an older one if the app permits.
- Businesses generally need merchant QR codes, checkout integration and reconciliation tools in addition to a shareable UPI ID.


UPI has become one of India’s most widely used digital payment systems. Whether you are receiving money from customers, paying a bill or sending money to a friend, your UPI ID acts as your digital payment address.


This guide explains what a UPI ID means, how it works, how to create and find one, how to change a UPI ID in Google Pay, and the safety checks every user should follow.


##


What Is a UPI ID?


A UPI ID, or Unified Payments Interface ID, is a unique identifier used to send and receive money through the UPI network without entering a bank account number and IFSC code for every transaction. It is also known as a[Virtual Payment Address or VPA](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/vpa-in-upi/) .


**A typical UPI ID looks like:**


- yourname@oksbi
- businessname@paytm
- 1234567890@ybl


The part before` @` identifies the user, while the part after it is the UPI handle associated with a payment service provider bank. The handle does not necessarily indicate where the user’s bank account is held.


When someone sends money to a valid UPI ID, the payment is routed to the bank account currently linked to it. Think of a UPI ID as an email address for payments: it tells the UPI network where the money should go without exposing the complete bank account details.


##


Is a UPI ID the Same as a UPI ID Number?


People often search for a “UPI ID number,” but a standard UPI ID is generally an alphanumeric address containing an` @` handle. A UPI Number is a separate bank-verified, 8 to 10-digit alias that may be a mobile number or another chosen number.


Both can be used to locate a recipient, but they are not the same identifier. If an app asks for a UPI ID, enter the complete address such as` name@bankhandle` , not only a phone number unless the app specifically supports UPI Number payments.


##


How Does a UPI ID Work?


When you create a UPI ID through a UPI-enabled app, it is mapped to a bank account. Instead of entering lengthy bank details, the sender can use this ID to initiate a transfer.


The payment process works as follows:


1. The sender enters the recipient’s UPI ID or scans a QR code.
2. The UPI system resolves the ID and displays the recipient’s name.
3. The sender checks the name and amount before continuing.
4. The sender authorises the payment using a UPI PIN in their own app.
5. The participating banks process the transfer, usually within seconds.


The ID identifies the destination, while the UPI PIN authorises money leaving the sender’s account. For a broader explanation of the network, see[how UPI works in India](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/upi-full-form-meaning-how-it-works/) .


***Also Read:[How UPI Payment Gateway Integration Works for Websites and Apps](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/upi-integration/)***


##


Why Do You Need a UPI ID?


A UPI ID simplifies digital payments by acting as a secure payment address linked to your bank account.


**Benefits include:**


- Receive money without sharing account numbers or[IFSC codes](https://www.cashfree.com/IFSC-verification-api/) .
- Send money instantly to individuals and businesses.
- Make payments across multiple banks and UPI apps.
- Maintain privacy by avoiding direct sharing of banking details.
- Manage personal and business transactions separately.
- [Accept payments through QR codes](https://www.cashfree.com/upi-qr-code/) , payment links, and online checkouts.


For businesses, a professional UPI ID can improve customer trust and make payment collection more organized.


##


How to Create a UPI ID


You can create a UPI ID through any[NPCI-approved UPI app such as Google Pay, PhonePe, Paytm, BHIM](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/top-upi-apps-in-india/) , or your bank’s mobile banking application. In most cases, a UPI ID is automatically generated when you link your bank account, though some apps allow you to create additional custom IDs.


**Given below are the steps to create your UPI ID** :


1. Download and install a UPI enabled app (e.g. Google Pay, phonepe, Paytm, bhim, bank app)
2. Register your mobile number which is connected to your bank account
3. Link your bank account to the app
4. Verify your account via OTP
5. Set your UPI pin using debit card details and OTP
6. Generate/confirm your own customized UPI ID


Once setup is complete, you can start sending and receiving payments instantly.


***Also read:[What is UPI? Full Form, Meaning, Features & How UPI Works in India](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/upi-full-form-meaning-how-it-works/)***


##


**How to Find Your UPI ID**


Your UPI ID is generally available under the profile, bank account or payment settings section of the app. The exact path varies.


In most apps:


1. Open the UPI app.
2. Go to your profile or payment methods.
3. Select the linked bank account.
4. Open the UPI ID or Manage UPI IDs option.
5. Copy the ID you want to share.


An account may have more than one UPI ID, so check which one is active or marked for receiving payments.


##


**How to Change Your UPI ID**


You might need to update your existing UPI ID if it is too lengthy, difficult to remember, or not suitable for professional purposes. To modify your existing UPI ID follow these steps:


- **Step 1:** Open your UPI app.
- **Step 2:** Click on the Profile / Payment Settings / Bank Account Details.
- **Step 3:** Locate Add / Create New UPI ID option.
- **Step 4:** Select an available UPI ID.
- **Step 5:** Save the updated ID and mark it as Primary if allowed by the App.


Some apps may limit editing an existing ID. In those situations, you can usually add another ID and use it instead of modifying the original one.


***Also read:[GPay Transaction Limit Per Day](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/google-pay-transaction-limit/)***


##


**Can You Have More Than One UPI ID?**


Yes. Many apps allow multiple UPI IDs to be linked to the same bank account. This can improve payment routing and lets users keep different shareable addresses.


Multiple IDs may be useful for:


- Keeping one ID for personal payments
- Using a separate ID for public-facing or business collections
- Replacing an ID that contains a mobile number
- Maintaining an alternative route if one payment service provider is temporarily unavailable


The number of IDs and management options depend on the app. Separate IDs linked to the same bank account do not create separate bank accounts or balances.


##


UPI ID vs UPI Number vs UPI PIN


**Feature** **UPI ID** **UPI Number** **UPI PIN**


Purpose Identifies a payment destination Numeric alias for finding a UPI user Authorises a debit from an account


Format` name@handle` Bank-verified 8 to 10-digit number Confidential 4 or 6-digit code


Can it be shared? Yes Yes No


Example` abc@oksbi` Mobile number or chosen number Never disclose an example PIN


Used for Sending or receiving money Sending or receiving money Approving outgoing payments or mandates


> **Important: No genuine bank, UPI app, or customer support executive will ever ask for your UPI PIN.**


##


**Tips for Choosing a Good UPI ID**


A good UPI ID should be:


- Simple and easy to remember.
- As short as possible.
- A professional id if used for business use.
- Not too personal or sensitive (use a name / brand for work).


A recognisable ID can make it easier to[accept UPI payments](https://www.cashfree.com/upi-payment-gateway/) , but the recipient name shown by the payer’s app is the more important trust check. Businesses should not rely on the text of the UPI ID alone to establish authenticity.


##


UPI ID Safety Tips


Follow these precautions when using UPI:


- Never share your UPI PIN, OTP or screen-sharing access.
- Verify the recipient’s name and amount before approving a payment.
- Reject collect requests you do not recognise.
- Do not scan a QR code to receive money. Scanning and entering a PIN normally initiates a payment.
- Avoid payment links from untrusted sources.
- Use an app lock or supported biometric security.
- Keep the UPI app and phone operating system updated.
- Check the final transaction status instead of relying only on a screenshot.


NPCI’s[UPI Safety Shield](https://www.npci.org.in/safety-feature) confirms that a UPI PIN is required to deduct money, not to receive it.


> **Remember:** If someone asks you to enter a UPI PIN to receive a payment, refund or reward, treat it as a likely scam.


For wider precautions covering payment requests and account takeovers, see this guide to[identifying and preventing payment fraud](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/fraudulent-transactions-how-to-identify-and-prevent/) .


##


How Businesses Use UPI IDs for Collections


For a small seller, a shareable UPI ID may be enough for occasional collections. Businesses handling regular order volume generally need additional controls for customer experience, payment confirmation and reconciliation.


**Businesses commonly use UPI IDs alongside:**


- Dynamic and static QR codes
- [Payment links](https://www.cashfree.com/payment-links/)
- Checkout pages
- Subscription payments ([UPI Autopay](https://www.cashfree.com/upi-autopay/) )
- Invoice-based collections


Solutions such as Cashfree Payments help businesses manage UPI collections,[payment reconciliation](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/reconciling-your-payment/) , settlement tracking, and customer payment experiences at scale.


### Conclusion


A UPI ID is the payment address that helps users send and receive money without repeatedly sharing bank account details. It is different from a UPI Number and, most importantly, from the confidential UPI PIN used to authorise outgoing payments.


Whether you use UPI for personal transfers or business collections, verify the recipient name, reject unknown collect requests and never enter a PIN to receive money. Businesses processing regular orders should also use payment-status tracking and reconciliation rather than relying on screenshots or manual confirmation.

##


**FAQs**


#### What is an example of a UPI ID?


A UPI ID can look like yourname@oksbi, business@paytm or number@ybl, depending on the app and payment service provider handle.


#### Can one bank account have multiple UPI IDs?


Yes. Many UPI apps allow multiple IDs to be linked to the same bank account. The permitted number and available handles depend on the app and participating banks.


#### **Is it safe to share my UPI ID?**


It is generally safe to share a UPI ID for receiving money. However, sharing it may lead to unsolicited collect requests, and the payer can normally see the recipient name. Never share the UPI PIN.


#### **What happens if I send money to the wrong UPI ID?**


If the ID is valid and the transaction succeeds, the money may reach the unintended recipient. Report the transaction immediately through the UPI app and contact your bank. A successful UPI payment cannot always be reversed automatically.


#### **Why is my UPI ID not showing in the app?**


The bank account may not be linked correctly, mobile-number verification may be incomplete, or the bank or app may be experiencing an issue. Update the app, check the registered SIM and reopen the linked account settings.


#### **Can I receive money through UPI without sharing my phone number?**


Yes. You can usually share an alphanumeric UPI ID or QR code instead. Avoid an ID containing your mobile number if keeping the number private is important.


#### **Can someone withdraw money using only my UPI ID?**


No. A UPI ID alone does not authorise a debit. Money can leave your account only after an authorised payment, mandate or collect request is approved using the required authentication.


#### **Why do I receive payment requests after sharing my UPI ID?**


Anyone who knows the ID may be able to send a collect request. Read the payer, payee and amount carefully, and reject any request you do not recognise.


#### **What should I do if UPI payments keep failing?**


Check the UPI PIN, account balance, bank limits, network connection and app version. Bank downtime, expired requests and temporary routing issues can also cause failures. See the guide to[common online payment failures](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/why-do-online-payments-fail/) for additional troubleshooting.
